o1.biggest_strength: It is built directly from our data: on-feet workers first, problem hooks first, mission as the close, and a $38 new-customer target tied to 90-day contribution.
o1.biggest_mistake: The day-20 release rules mix TikTok-reported CPA, store tags, and survey reads in a slightly fuzzy way, and the holdout idea may be noisy for only 30 days.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the measurement rules so the team knows exactly which source wins when reads disagree, and add the exact creator brief/output owners for the next 6 to 10 worker creators.

o2.biggest_strength: It gets the main strategic call right: lead with real worker comfort, use the nurse and server Spark Ads, avoid discount and mission-first hooks, and judge against a $38 target.
o2.biggest_mistake: It is a little more generic and less disciplined operationally: scaling/Smart+ starts early, the day-30 scorecard leans more on TikTok-claimed orders than I would like, and some rules are not as tightly tied to the economics.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the budget phasing and scale rules more conservative until tracking is proven, remove Smart+ from month one, and make the final decision rule primarily Shopify new customers plus survey/lift against the $38 90-day break-even.

reason: Output 1 feels more like a plan I could hand to the team Monday morning: the numbers are sharper, the budget adds up cleanly, and the creative plan follows the actual signals in our data. Output 2 is good, but it needs more tightening before I would trust it with the full $30,000.
